content: Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic agent approved by the FDA for use in surgical hand rubs and aseptic handwashing. It is effective in significantly reducing the number of microorganisms on the hands and forearms before surgery or patient care. Common adverse reactions include contact dermatitis and other dermatological manifestations. For surgical hand scrubbing, jewelry should be removed, and nails should be cleaned with an orangewood stick. Hands and forearms should be wetted with water, and 5 mL of the product should be applied. The hands and forearms should be washed and scrubbed for 5 minutes, paying particular attention to nails, cuticles, and interdigital spaces, followed by thorough rinsing with water. Alternatively, hands and forearms can be wetted, and a palmful of the product can be dispensed to the hands. Scrubbing should last for 20 seconds, followed by thorough rinsing and drying. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of povidone-iodine in both adult and pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Similarly, there is limited information on its use in pediatric patients for FDA-labeled indications. Povidone-iodine is contraindicated for use in the eyes and is intended for external use only. If the product comes into contact with the eyes, it should be rinsed promptly and thoroughly with water. Use should be discontinued if irritation or redness develops, and a doctor should be consulted if these symptoms persist for more than 72 hours. The product should be kept out of reach of children, and if swallowed, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. Adverse reactions reported include contact dermatitis. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experiences, drug interactions, and monitoring of povidone-iodine. Additionally, there is no FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric, geriatric, or specific gender or racial populations. Similarly, no guidance exists for its use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, or in immunocompromised individuals. Povidone-iodine is administered topically. There is limited information on its pharmacology, including its mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. Information on clinical studies, supply, storage, and patient counseling is also limited. The interaction between alcohol and povidone-iodine has not been established. Patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication.
